target_customer: Enterprise and academic research labs that run instruments from vendors such as Bruker, Thermo Fisher Scientific and Waters
problem: Lab data sits in instruments, spreadsheets and notes in inconsistent formats, so researchers cannot search it or use AI on it.
business_model: B2B SaaS data infrastructure for labs (pricing not public)
product_category: Scientific data infrastructure and lab data capture

founders.name: Connor Hogan
founders.background_notes: Per the YC launch post, worked on database products at Google. Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Caitlin Hogan
prior_employers: A materials science startup (name not given), four years leading data infrastructure
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page and launch post. Described by a search summary as a sibling of Connor, which is not confirmed on a page I opened.

competitors.name: TetraScience
competitors.what: Scientific data cloud that captures and harmonizes instrument data for pharma and biotech
competitors.traction_then: Established vendor with a large connector library and a Benchling integration

competitors.name: Scitara
competitors.what: Instrument connectivity and lab data integration platform

competitors.name: Benchling
competitors.what: R&D cloud for biotech that connects instrument data to scientific records

technical_complexity.rationale: Capturing data from many proprietary instrument formats and cleaning it is integration heavy, but uses standard engineering. The CTO had four years building lab data infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Instrument integrations and accumulated structured data could create lock-in, but incumbents like TetraScience and Scitara already hold large connector libraries.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. Benchling positioned itself as a lab orchestration layer connecting instruments by 2025.

market_need_then: Labs generate data in fragmented formats and the AI wave in 2025 raised demand for clean, structured research data. No spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses labric.co, not the .com, as of 2025 per the company website.

identity.visual_style: Professional lab imagery over gradient backgrounds, per the site as read
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and professional with short headlines such as Designed for how labs actually operate

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand itself was found. It is a new company with a plain site.

outcome_analysis: Labric is a very young company from Spring 2025 with no reported exit, layoffs or shutdown. It sells into a crowded lab data space with established vendors, and its main assets are a CTO with direct lab data infrastructure experience and the timing of AI demand for structured data. No traction or round figures could be verified, so the outcome is open.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked and Caplight (aggregators only) list about $500K total in June 2025, with Caplight naming Y Combinator and Kleiner Perkins. Not recorded as a round. YC pages label the batch inconsistently (X25, P25); the directory says Spring 2025. No outcome news found. Completeness pass: Round rests on a single database (VCBacked, which names only Y Combinator; Caplight also lists Kleiner Perkins as an accelerator entry, not recorded as an investor). No press release found.
